author: ValWood
body:
Apologies. I was just enquiring about the procedure, to decide how to query the annotation.

This one seemed odd because Tim54 wasn't a kinase as far as I was aware.
but I see  there is a reported DGK domain in human

I don't think it is conclusive based on the evidence  that this is physiologically;y relevant:
2017 summary:

https://www.cell.com/molecular-cell/fulltext/S1097-2765(17)30441-0?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS1097276517304410%3Fshowall%3Dtrue 

"Although AGK contains a highly conserved DGK domain, the human and murine proteins segregate away from the other lipid
kinase families (Waggoner et al., 2004). However, several lines of evidence **suggest** that AGK has a dual role as a genuine acylglycerol kinase: AGK can catalyze the phosphorylation of both MAG
and DAG in vitro, producing LPA and PA (Bektas et al., 2005); bacterially expressed AGK protein can phosphorylate MAG
and DAG (Waggoner et al., 2004); downregulation of AGK reduces intracellular levels of LPA and PA (Bektas et al., 2005);
overexpression of AGK in cells increases cellular levels of LPA and PA (Bektas et al., 2005); and overexpression of a kinasedead mutant of AGK did not increase AGK activity or produce LPA (Bektas et al., 2005). However, expression of a kinasedead mutant in AGKKO revealed that AGK’s kinase activity is not required for the protein’s function at the TIM22 complex.
AGKG126E-expressing cells displayed a restoration in the steady-state levels of TIM22 complex subunits (hTim22 and
Tim29) and carrier substrates (GC1 and ANT3) as well as in the assembly of the TIM22 complex itself and assembly of the carrier proteins GC1, PiC, and ANT. This indicates that AGK has both a kinase-dependent function (Bektas et al., 2005; Waggoner et al., 2004) and a kinase-independent function within mitochondria

mainly  in vitro assay and expression related
but it should stand  unless  there is conclusive evidence that it isn't.
(this is just for reference if I come across it again)
